$comment: Pins the Go and TypeScript schema validators to one another on JSON Schema `format`. Both harnesses read this file, build the same one-property schema per case in each dialect, and must produce the recorded verdict. Only the formats the HDF schemas actually assert are listed — see formats[] — because those are the ones a converter test's input-validity guard depends on. Adding a format here is a deliberate act: it changes what every existing test accepts. A case states `valid` when the two libraries agree, or `go` and `ts` when they do not; see divergences[] for why any case does the latter. The formats in tsAnnotationOnly[] are ones ajv-formats does not implement: TypeScript registers them as annotation-only and accepts every value, so their rows always spell `go` and `ts` — `valid` there would dress one side's silence up as agreement.

divergences.summary: Go's libraries accept characters RFC 3986 excludes; ajv rejects them.
divergences.detail: santhosh-tekuri (2020-12) and gojsonschema (draft-07) both accept a space, '<', '|', '^' and backtick inside a uri-reference. ajv-formats rejects all five. Neither side is RFC 3986-exact: ajv accepts a double quote, which the RFC also excludes, and rejects malformed percent-encoding that a character-level check would pass. Matching one library to the other would import its idiosyncrasies rather than make either correct, so the divergence is recorded and tested instead — if a library upgrade changes either verdict, these cases fail and the next contributor sees this note. The seven other formats agree exactly, including uuid and date-time, the two that actually produced a false-green test.

divergences.summary: ajv-formats does not implement them; TypeScript registers them as annotation-only and asserts nothing, so only the Go harness can catch a violation.
divergences.detail: ajv-formats 3.x ships no iri, iri-reference, idn-email or idn-hostname and points at the ajv-formats-draft2019 plugin, last published in 2022 on top of uri-js, the URI library ajv itself replaced with fast-uri — not a maintained implementation. Nor is Go's check RFC 3987: santhosh-tekuri aliases iri to its uri validator and iri-reference to uri-reference (net/url plus an IPv6-host check) and has no idn-email at all, so its 2020-12 path is as blind to idn-email as ajv; gojsonschema aliases iri and iri-reference to its URI checkers and idn-email to net/mail. Aliasing iri to ajv's own uri would reject the non-ASCII IRIs Go accepts (ajv's uri regex is ASCII-only), so the two harnesses would disagree while claiming to check the same thing. The gap is recorded instead: tsAnnotationOnly[] names the set, schema-validation.ts registers exactly that set as always-valid, and any other format ajv-formats lacks fails schema compilation until it is added here deliberately. A converter whose schema uses one of these — hdf-to-openvex (iri on every @id), hdf-to-cyclonedx-vex (iri-reference on url fields, idn-email on contacts) — says so in its TypeScript schema test: that suite's green proves nothing about IRI shape or address syntax.

$resolved: gojsonschema's built-in uuid and date-time checkers were wrong four ways — rejecting an uppercase uuid and a lowercase RFC 3339 t, rejecting a legal leap second, and accepting a bare date as a date-time. hdf-validators now replaces both at gojsonschema's process-global registry, so this harness's draft-07 path inherits the corrected behaviour whenever hdf-validators is linked (its own test binary imports it). The `goDraft07` field remains supported for a future case that needs it.

cases.why: RFC 4122 §3: readers accept either case. gojsonschema's built-in checker rejected this until hdf-validators replaced it
the padded-uuid case that exposed the divergence: accepted by Go, rejected by ajv
RFC 3339 permits a space separator only by mutual agreement; HDF's canonical form requires T, so ajv is tightened to match Go
a date-time is not a date
uri requires a scheme; uri-reference does not
a percent-encoded space is the correct spelling of the divergent case below
both accept a double quote, which RFC 3986 excludes — recorded so the shared lenience is visible, not just the divergent one
a purl, the product id shape OpenVEX documents actually carry
a legal IRI that is not a legal URI: ajv's uri check rejects it, which is why iri is not aliased to it
the bare product id hdf-to-openvex once minted: relative, so not an IRI. Only Go caught it
an empty reference is a legal same-document reference; neither side rejects it
a space in the host, unlike one in the path, is a parse error for net/url
a backslash is the one character both Go libraries reject in a reference
the internationalised address idn-email exists for; net/mail accepts it
santhosh-tekuri has no idn-email, so 2020-12 Go accepts it too; only gojsonschema — draft-07, the dialect CycloneDX 1.4 declares — rejects it
